title: City bus ticketing modernization
summary: A metropolitan transit authority is deciding how to modernize fare payment without disrupting service or excluding riders who still rely on cash or legacy transit cards.

sections.title: Situation
sections.narrative: The current network depends on cash and closed-loop plastic transit cards. The proposed modernization would introduce app-based payment and open-loop contactless acceptance while keeping buses in service throughout the transition.

entries.text: full open-loop contactless payment with bank cards and phones
legal approval for account-based fare processing
buses must continue operating without downtime
elderly and unbanked riders must not be excluded
policy boundary around inclusion and privacy
direct shift to open-loop bank-card payment

candidate_paths.title: Path A: conservative modernization
candidate_paths.narrative: This path is operationally robust and politically safer, but it extends the transition period and retains more legacy complexity.
highlights: add compatibility and inspection tools before broad rollout
preserve access for riders without bank cards
keep coordination burden lower during the early stages

candidate_paths.title: Path B: coordinated leap
candidate_paths.narrative: This path has the highest performance upside, but it is more fragile if external readiness or governance approval slips.
highlights: move directly to account-based contactless payment
depend on banking integration, legal approval, and stronger multi-party coordination
